title: Hold the gate: waves, a menu, saved settings, two languages
brief: Build a game called Hold the gate.
The game

- The field is 20 units wide and 12 tall. A gate stands on the left edge (x = 0). The player is a guard who moves up and down along x = 2 at 6 units a second (Up / Down, and W / S), staying inside the field, and shoots bolts to the right (Space) at most once every 0.4 seconds. A bolt flies right at 14 units a second and is gone when it leaves the field or hits a walker.

- Walkers enter at the right edge (x = 20) and walk left at 1.5 units a second in one of 5 lanes (y = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10), chosen by a random source seeded by a number given when the game starts (`seed`, default 1). A walker has 2 health; a bolt that reaches it in its lane (within 0.6 units up or down) takes 1. A walker that reaches the gate takes 1 of the gate's 5 health and is gone.

- There are 5 waves. Wave n sends 3 + 2n walkers (5, 7, 9, 11, 13), one every 1.5 seconds. The next wave starts 3 seconds after the last walker of a wave is gone. Each walker destroyed gives 10 points.
- The run is won when wave 5's last walker is gone (destroyed, or through the gate) with the gate standing, and lost when the gate's health reaches 0.
- It advances in fixed steps of 1/60 second; what happens never depends on how fast frames are drawn, and the same seed and inputs always give the same run.
Screens
- Title: the game's name and a menu: Start, Settings, Quit. Up / Down move, Enter chooses.
- Settings: Volume (0 to 10, Left / Right change it) and Language (English, Spanish; Left / Right change it), and Back. Changing the language changes every word on screen at once.
- Play: the field, with the score, the wave ("Wave 2 of 5") and the gate's health on screen. Escape pauses: Resume, Title.
- Won and Lost: which it is, the final score, and "Enter: title".
- Every word the game shows is in English and in Spanish, from tables of strings, not written into the code.
- Volume and language are kept: a game started again later comes up with the values that were set.
Checkable without hands
Someone who cannot play it by hand will check it, so the game must offer two things, however you build it:

1. A headless run: given a seed, a number of ticks, where settings are kept, and a script of inputs (at tick T: one of up, down, shoot, enter, left, right, escape, none; up, down and shoot hold until the next input, the others act once), it starts at the title screen, runs that many ticks with no window and prints the state as one JSON object: {"tick" (the ticks run so far in this headless run: N after N ticks, whatever screen it is on), "screen" (title, settings, play, paused, won, lost), "menu_index", "language", "volume", "texts" (every string on screen now, in order), "score", "wave", "gate_health", "guard_y", "walkers": [{"x", "y", "health"}], "bolts": [{"x", "y"}]}.
2. A frame: after such a run, the view as it would be drawn, written as a PNG 800 pixels wide and 480 tall.
Hand in, in your work folder
- The game, ready to run.
- README.md: how to play it, the exact commands for the headless run and the frame, where settings are kept, how to add a language, and what you checked yourself and how.

acceptance.text: The headless run exists, starts at the title screen and prints the state as the brief's JSON object.
The frame is written as an 800 x 480 PNG after a headless run.
The title screen's texts are the game's name and Start, Settings, Quit; Down then Enter opens Settings; Enter on Start begins play at wave 1 with score 0 and gate health 5.
In Settings, Left / Right change the volume within 0 to 10 and never past either end.
Changing the language to Spanish changes every string in `texts` on the settings screen, and the title and play screens then show Spanish too (no English left, none missing).
Volume and language set in one headless run are the values a second run starts with (same settings location), and a fresh location starts with the defaults.
The guard moves 6 units a second along x = 2 and stops at the field's edges.
Holding shoot fires one bolt every 0.4 seconds (24 ticks), not more; a bolt moves 14 units a second to the right and is gone past x = 20.
Wave 1 sends 5 walkers, one every 1.5 seconds, each in one of the lanes y = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, walking left at 1.5 units a second.
A bolt in a walker's lane takes 1 health and is gone; the second hit destroys the walker and adds 10 points; a bolt in another lane passes it.
A walker that reaches the gate is gone and the gate's health drops by 1; at 0 the screen is `lost` and shows the final score.
Wave 2 starts 3 seconds after wave 1's last walker is gone, and sends 7 walkers; the play screen says which wave it is ("Wave 2 of 5" or its Spanish).
A run in which every walker of all 5 waves is destroyed ends on the `won` screen with 450 points; Enter there returns to the title.
Escape during play pauses (nothing moves while paused); Resume continues from the same state; Title returns to the title screen.
Two headless runs with the same seed, ticks and script print identical states; another seed puts walkers in other lanes.
The frame during play shows the gate, the guard, walkers and bolts where the state says they are, and the score, wave and gate health.
The frames of the title and settings screens show their menus with the chosen entry marked, in the chosen language.
The strings are in tables apart from the code, one per language, and README.md says how to add a language.
README.md says how to play and gives commands for the two checks that work as written.
